ui_bugs.issue: Wrong PIN displays generic 'HTTP 403' instead of API-provided 'PIN salah' in [data-testid="staff-gate-error"]. Backend returns {detail:'PIN salah'} (curl-verified). Suspect StrictMode double-invoke of auto-submit useEffect causes one fetch's res.json() to succeed (sets detail='PIN salah') and a second concurrent fetch's res.json() to either fail or be parsed before body is fully buffered, with the catch path falling back to `HTTP ${res.status}`. Functional gate behavior (stays up, inputs cleared, no leak) is correct — only the error string is wrong.

action_items: [LOW] In /app/frontend/src/components/auth/StaffPinGate.jsx tryUnlock(): guard against StrictMode double-invoke and/or fix the j.detail parsing fallback. Recommended fix: add a useRef inFlightRef guard at top of tryUnlock (similar to ClockOutModal pattern from iter_17) to prevent the second concurrent fetch. Also consider parsing the body once via res.text() then JSON.parse in a try/catch to make the fallback more resilient. Alternatively, read body BEFORE the (!res.ok) check failure path to guarantee the response stream is captured cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: Spec-permitted but worth flagging: /api/auth/me does NOT re-check the OWNER_EMAILS whitelist against the looked-up user. If a non-whitelisted email's session record exists in Mongo (e.g. via seed/manual insert), /me will return that user with 200. The whitelist is only enforced at /api/auth/session exchange time. This is acceptable per the request spec but is a defense-in-depth gap. Consider adding a whitelist check in /me to harden against direct DB tampering.

OwnerProtectedRoute does not re-validate user.email against OWNER_EMAILS on the frontend either. Anyone with a forged session_token whose backing user.email is non-whitelisted would be admitted by the frontend. Same root cause as above.

Auth cookie is configured with secure=True + samesite='none' + httpOnly=True — correct for the cross-site preview Cloudflare ingress. Verified that /auth/logout's response.delete_cookie() works in conjunction with Mongo session delete; the /me call after logout returns 401 as expected.
Recharts width(-1)/height(-1) console warnings on /admin and /dashboard come from PipelineDashboard's chart container before the layout settles — purely cosmetic, no functional impact.

rca of the issue: PIN-wrong error-text mismatch RCA: Backend confirmed correct via `curl -X POST /api/auth/staff-pin -d '{"pin_code":"9999"}'` → HTTP 403 body `{"detail":"PIN salah"}` (Cloudflare passthrough, content-type application/json, content-length 22). Frontend StaffPinGate.jsx tryUnlock() reads `let detail = `HTTP ${res.status}`; try { const j = await res.json(); detail = j.detail || detail; } catch (e) {}` — should yield 'PIN salah'. The most likely culprit is React 18 StrictMode double-invoking the auto-submit useEffect, causing two concurrent POSTs whose Response bodies race; one of them (probably the second) fails res.json() and falls into the silent catch, leaving detail at the `HTTP ${res.status}` fallback, which then overwrites the first call's correct error via setError. Fix is to add an `inFlightRef` useRef guard at the top of tryUnlock (mirroring the ClockOutModal firedRef pattern landed in iter_17 for AttendanceKiosk.jsx). Alternative: drop the `if (submitting) return;` closure-stale check and rely solely on the ref. Reproduction steps: open https://laundrymax-cashier.preview.emergentagent.com/, sessionStorage.clear(), reload, type 9999 → observe banner reads 'HTTP 403' (expected 'PIN salah'). Mitigation: low priority — does not break auth, only the user-facing error string is generic instead of localized.
